question: Using the customary setting of the mathematics used for quantum mechanics, is it possible to prove the existence of Gödelßs god-like entities?

2.text:
In the Hilbert space/C*-algebra formalism the physical content of
quantum mechanics is a theory in the ordinary classical meta-theory
ZFC + first order arithmetic. That meta-theory is able to talk about
first order modal languages and about formal proofs in them, and hence
it is able to write down Gödel's derivation formally.

What Gödel shows is a theorem of the modal propositional first order
logic S5 together with the purely metaphysical ontological axioms

* P is positive, P → □P for every positive P,
* P is positive iff ¬P is not positive, 
* If P is positive and P → Q then Q is positive,
* Necessary existence is positive,

etc., of the form

NecEssentiallyExistent → ∃x □Ex,  and hence ∃x Gx

where Gx is the conjunction of all positive properties.  The
derivation is a derivation in S5.  It is not a derivation in the
Hilbert space axioms, it is not a derivation in the linear algebra
of observables, it is not a statement about spectra, expectation
values, transition amplitudes or any other quantity that occurs in
quantum mechanics. 

The modal operators □, the notion of a positive property and the
concept of necessary existence are extrinsic to the mathematics of
a complex Hilbert space, of self-adjoint operators and of the
spectral theorem.  The proof therefore does not produce a
consequence of quantum theory.  At best it can be reproduced as a
piece of first order mathematics in the set-theoretic background in
which the Hilbert space formalism lives. The conclusion is then
conditional on the acceptance of the ontological axioms and of the
S5 semantics, which are not theorems of, nor even expressible in, the
physical formalism of QM.  In the physical sense there is no
quantum-mechanical proof of the existence of a Gödelian god-like
entity; one only reproduces a purely formal, essentially
metaphysical, conditional argument in the classical meta-language
that happens also to be the meta-language of quantum mechanics.
∎

4.text:
In the customary literature the mathematics that is used for ordinary
non-relativistic quantum mechanics is just the ordinary classical
mathematics of analysis: a complex separable Hilbert space
${\cal H}$, self–adjoint operators on ${\cal H}$, the spectral theorem
etc.  That is ZFC + real/complex analysis. That is the same formal
system in which first order modal logic and therefore Gödel’s
ontological argument can be written down.

Gödel’s argument is

* G1  $\phi$ is positive $\to$ $\square \phi$ is positive,
* G2  $\phi$ is positive $\to$ $\phi$ is consistent,
* G3  $\phi_{1},...,\phi_{n}$ positive $\to$ $\exists x\bigwedge_{i}\phi_{i}(x)$
is consistent,

together with the S5 modal logic and the definition
$P(x)\equiv \bigwedge\{\phi(x):\phi$ positive$\}$.

From these purely formal premises one obtains in S5

${\rm Provable}\; \diamond \exists xP(x) \rightarrow \square \exists xP(x)$

and with the axiom that necessary existence is positive,
$\square\exists x\phi(x)$ positive, the familiar

$\exists xP(x)$

i.e. a being with all positive properties exists necessarily.
That derivation is a theorem of the classical first order
theory in which Hilbert-space quantum mechanics is written.  In
that purely syntactic sense the argument can be reproduced in the
mathematical framework of quantum theory.

The derivation is conditional and non-empirical. The positivity
axioms, the S5 necessitation rule and the identification of
‘positive property’ with ‘desirable metaphysical property’ are
metaphysical premises, they are not theorems of analysis,
Hilbert-space theory or of any physical theory.  Accepting them
you get a formal consistency proof of a God-like maximally great
being, i.e. a being with all positive properties in the sense of
the axioms.  That is not a physical or empirical proof of the
existence of such an entity in the world, and it does not become a
consequence of the mathematical formalism of quantum mechanics,
which is descriptive of physical states and observables.  In the
ordinary ontological sense the existence does not follow from the
mathematics used in QM.

In the physics literature the formalism of non-relativistic quantum mechanics is
the separable complex Hilbert space $H$, the lattice of closed subspaces of $H$
and the (essentially) self-adjoint operators on $H$ together with the usual
set-theoretic first order mathematics in which that is written down.  In
particular the language that is used for the physics is the language of
classical first order set theory, analysis and linear algebra over ${\mathbb C}$.
It contains no modal operator $ \Box ,\Diamond $, no predicate
$P(x)$ ``$P$ is a positive property'', no predicate $G(x)$ ``$x$ is God-like'',
and no axioms of the form

* $P(x)\to \Box P(x)$,
* $P(x)\wedge (P(x)\to Q(x))\to Q(x)$, etc.

Gödel's ontological argument is a theorem of the modal propositional
calculus $S5$ together with the five – six – metaphysical axioms on
positivity and the definition

$$G(x)\equiv \forall P\,[P(x)\to P \hbox{ is positive}]$$

and the axiom that existence is a positive property.  The theorem is
$ \exists x\, G(x)$ and, in the usual formulation, $\,\Box \exists x\, G(x)$.
The argument is therefore a theorem of modal logic, not a theorem of
Hilbert-space theory, functional analysis or the usual set-theoretic
real number calculus that is used in quantum mechanics.

In the ordinary physical formalism there is simply no interpretation of
`necessarily', `positive property' or `God-like' and hence no way to even
state the Gödel axioms, let alone derive $\exists x\,G(x)$ from the
Hilbert-space calculus.  If the underlying set theory in which the
Hilbert space is defined is taken as a meta-theory, $S5$ can of course be
encoded in ordinary higher order set theory and the Gödel derivation can
be transcribed as a purely formal derivation in ZFC.  That is a transcription
of a modal-metaphysical proof into set theory; it is not a proof that lives
inside the customary quantum-mechanical language of vectors, operators and
spectra, and it brings in precisely the non-physical modal and
metaphysical premises that the customary mathematics of quantum mechanics
does not contain.  In physical terms the existence of a Gödel God-like
entity is therefore not a consequence of, and cannot be proved in, the
Hilbert-space formalism that is ordinarily used for quantum mechanics.

3.text:
In the customary physics literature quantum mechanics is done in ordinary
classical mathematics, viz. a Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory with the
usual analysis and functional analysis on complex Hilbert spaces over it.
That set-theoretic background is perfectly adequate to formalize first
order modal logic and in particular the modal logic S5 in which Godel
wrote his ontological argument. In that sense the argument can be
re-expressed as a derivation in the meta-theory that underlies the
Hilbert space formalism.

What it cannot be is a theorem of the mathematics of quantum mechanics
proper. The mathematics of QM has no primitive for ‘property’, for
‘positive property’, for essence and for necessary existence. Godel’s
proof is

1. P is positive  →  ¬P is not positive,
2. If P is positive then necessarily P is positive,
3. If P is positive then necessarily P is positive →  Possibly P,
4. ... and the definition of God as the being that has every positive
   property,

from which in S5 one gets
∃x God x.

All of the premises (1)–(4) and the definition of a positive property are
metaphysical, not arithmetical or analytic. They are not theorems of ZF,
of functional analysis, nor of the spectral theory of self-adjoint
operators which is the working mathematics of quantum mechanics. They can
be taken as extra-logical axioms in a formalism that lives on top of ZF,
and with those axioms S5 yields the conditional statement

AxiomsG → ∃x God x,

in the set-theoretic background in which Hilbert spaces are defined.
That is a formalization of Godel’s argument, not a mathematical proof of
the existence of a Godelian god-like entity from physics-mathematics
alone. The existence claim remains conditional on the disputed
ontological axioms about positivity and necessary existence, which lie
outside the empirical/mathematical language of quantum mechanics. In the
strict sense the entity is not a mathematical object and its existence is
not provable within the mathematical formalism used for QM.
